play.title: Idle Tycoon: Borderline Empire
play.short: Truck delivery tycoon: grow a logistics empire across 8 fictional regions.

description:
Every empire starts with one rusty hatchback.

Borderline Empire is a casual idle tycoon game about running a delivery and logistics business in eight made-up countries. Meet Dot, a retired dispatcher who knows every back road, name your company, pick its colour and start taking the jobs nobody else wants. Fast routes pay more. Safe routes keep the heat down. You make the call.

RUN THE ROUTES
• Pick contracts, choose a vehicle and a route (Fast, Normal or Safe), then watch the delivery roll across a hand-crafted low-poly world.
• Handle surprises on the road: rival crews, inspections, breakdowns, road closures and nervous passengers.
• Keep each region's Heat in check, or the next border crossing gets a lot harder.
• Three daily logistics jobs with bonus rewards every day.

BUILD YOUR FLEET
• Collect and upgrade 10 vehicles, from the old hatchback to vans, pickups and box trucks: engine, capacity, navigation, suspension and more.
• Hire drivers with their own rarity and skills.
• Expand your headquarters from a dusty garage into a Logistics Center and an Underground HQ.
• Unlock 8 fictional regions, each with its own landscape, towns and border crossing.

AUTOMATE THE BUSINESS
• Auto Accept, Auto Assign and Auto Dispatch take over the routine work, then Regional Managers run whole regions while you plan.
• Earn Influence and spend it on permanent Connections.
• Reach Empire status, prestige and come back stronger with Legacy Stars.

MADE FOR SHORT BREAKS
• Satisfying 30-second sessions, with idle earnings while you're away.
• One-thumb portrait controls.
• Voiced mentor and announcer.
• Play without an account. Core gameplay works offline.
• Optional sponsor rewards and a one-time Empire Pass. No forced ads.

If you like truck games, delivery games, business and manager games or any idle tycoon, Borderline Empire gives you a whole transport empire to run from your pocket.

All countries, companies, people and goods in the game are fictional. Risk is shown only as numbers; there is no violence and no real-world locations.
